gaps: Open QA vendor mailboxes and verify each concerned vendor receives exactly one rejection email containing the buyer's reason
Verify no other vendor receives the rejection email and no real supplier receives any email

steps.note: Create a buyer-side event for the rejection scenario.
Use an RFQ stage so vendors can submit bids that the buyer can reject.
Apply the first available RFQ pricing template.
Add one line item for the vendor bids.
Commit a bidding schedule before publishing.
Invite two QA vendors so one can be rejected and the other can verify non-receipt.
Publish the event so vendors can bid.
Confirm the event is a real published project before bidding.
Submit a bid from the first QA vendor.
Confirm the first vendor's bid was accepted.
Submit a bid from a different QA vendor.
Confirm the second vendor's bid was accepted.
Close bidding so the buyer can process the submitted bids.

args.goal: On the buyer's Responses screen, reject exactly one submitted QA vendor bid using the buyer's rejection action, enter a buyer reason, submit the rejection, and stop when the screen shows the rejection succeeded.

steps.note: The catalog has no dedicated bid-rejection action, but the buyer can perform this on the Responses screen in the current session.

args.need: open the QA mailboxes for both invited vendors and verify that only the rejected vendor received exactly one rejection email containing the buyer's reason, while the other vendor and all real suppliers received none

steps.note: Mailbox access and email-recipient/content verification are outside the Procol screen catalog.
End with an observable assertion that the current screen remains healthy after the mailbox verification handoff.
